Scenario / Title: Host can start and test a meeting up to 7 days in advance
Preconditions: A Stream meeting is scheduled for a future date; current date is within 7 days before the scheduled start.
Steps:
1) Open the meeting from the platform/dashboard
2) Click Start/Test meeting (advance)
3) Enter the stream room
Expected Result: Host can enter a test session; stream is not publicly live to attendees unless explicitly started; UI indicates test mode if applicable.

Scenario / Title: Host is blocked from starting/testing earlier than 7 days in advance
Preconditions: A Stream meeting scheduled >7 days in the future; current date is earlier than allowed window.
Steps: 1) Attempt to Start/Test meeting
Expected Result: System blocks the action and shows a clear message about the 7-day advance limit.

Scenario / Title: Channel and stream are automatically created when host clicks Start meeting
Preconditions: Stream meeting exists; no channel/stream has been created yet for this meeting.
Steps:
1) Host clicks Start meeting
2) Observe provisioning behavior
3) Refresh/reopen meeting page
Expected Result: A channel/stream is created automatically and linked to the meeting; host lands in the live/test room; reloading does not create duplicates.

Scenario / Title: Idempotency: multiple rapid Start clicks do not create duplicate channels/streams
Preconditions: Stream meeting exists; host has access.
Steps:
1) Host clicks Start multiple times quickly (or open in 2 tabs and click Start)
2) Inspect meeting state
Expected Result: Only one channel/stream is created; host ends up in a single live session; no duplicate entries or errors.

Scenario / Title: Graceful error handling if auto provisioning fails
Preconditions: Simulate backend failure (if test environment supports) or invalid provisioning state.
Steps:
1) Host clicks Start meeting
2) Observe error handling and retry
Expected Result: Host sees actionable error message; retry works when backend recovers; system does not get stuck in partial state.

Scenario / Title: Attendee is placed in waiting room before live streaming starts
Preconditions: Meeting is scheduled; host has not started the live stream yet; attendee is eligible to join.
Steps:
1) Attendee attempts to join
2) Observe UI state
Expected Result: Attendee cannot view live stream yet; sees waiting room UI with clear messaging (e.g., “Waiting for host to start”).

Scenario / Title: When host starts live stream, attendees in waiting room transition to the live stream
Preconditions: One or more attendees are in waiting room; host is ready to go live.
Steps:
1) Host starts live
2) Attendee observes transition
3) Verify stream playback
Expected Result: Attendees are seamlessly moved from waiting room to live stream; playback starts; no manual refresh required (or a clear CTA is provided).

Scenario / Title: Attendee refreshes waiting room page and remains in waiting room (no bypass)
Preconditions: Host has not started live; attendee is in waiting room.
Steps:
1) Refresh the page
2) Observe state
Expected Result: Attendee remains in waiting room; cannot access live stream content before it starts.

Scenario / Title: Real-time stream supports webcams for up to 10 users concurrently
Preconditions: At least 11 eligible users can join; permissions allow camera use.
Steps:
1) Host starts meeting
2) Have 10 users enable webcams
3) User #11 attempts to enable webcam
Expected Result: System enforces the 10-webcam limit: user #11 is blocked or forced video-off with a clear message; existing 10 streams remain stable.

Scenario / Title: When one webcam stops, another user can start webcam (limit re-balances)
Preconditions: 10 webcams are currently active; user A turns webcam off.
Steps:
1) User A turns webcam off
2) User B turns webcam on
Expected Result: User B can enable webcam; total active webcams remain <=10.

Scenario / Title: Join with camera permission blocked: user can still watch stream and/or join without webcam
Preconditions: Browser camera permission = blocked; meeting is live.
Steps:
1) Join meeting
2) Try enabling camera
Expected Result: User can still participate in allowed ways; clear permission guidance is shown; no crash.

Scenario / Title: Host can control what content is shown on the main screen (webcams/content)
Preconditions: Meeting is live; at least 2 participants are present; host has control panel.
Steps:
1) Host selects a participant/camera to feature
2) Switch to shared content
3) Switch back
Expected Result: Main screen updates according to host selection; attendees see the same featured content; changes apply in near real-time.

Scenario / Title: Attendee cannot override host on-screen selection (if restricted)
Preconditions: Meeting is live; host has set featured content.
Steps: 1) Attendee attempts to change main screen selection
Expected Result: Attendee cannot override host selection; UI control is hidden/disabled; no unauthorized effect.

Scenario / Title: User joins after host has set featured content and sees the correct current on-screen state
Preconditions: Host already selected a featured participant/content; new attendee joins.
Steps:
1) Host sets featured content
2) New attendee joins
3) Observe on-screen content
Expected Result: Late joiner immediately sees the current featured content; no reset to defaults.

Scenario / Title: Host can share a webpage URL to the stream
Preconditions: Meeting is live; host has share controls.
Steps:
1) Host opens share
2) Select “Webpage/URL”
3) Enter a valid URL
4) Start sharing
Expected Result: Shared webpage is visible on main screen; attendees can see it clearly; stopping share returns to previous layout.

Scenario / Title: Host can share a video and attendees can see playback
Preconditions: Meeting is live; host has share controls; video source is supported.
Steps:
1) Start video share
2) Play/pause
3) Seek (if supported)
Expected Result: Attendees see the shared video; playback controls behave as designed; audio/video remain in sync per policy.

Scenario / Title: Host can share a presentation (file or slide) to the stream
Preconditions: Meeting is live; a supported presentation is available.
Steps:
1) Start presentation share
2) Navigate slides
3) Stop sharing
Expected Result: Slides render correctly; navigation updates what attendees see; stopping returns to prior view.

Scenario / Title: Invalid/blocked URL or unsupported content share shows clear error without breaking the stream
Preconditions: Meeting is live.
Steps:
1) Attempt to share an invalid URL or unsupported file
2) Observe error handling
Expected Result: Clear validation/error message; stream remains stable; user can try again.

Scenario / Title: Late joiner sees currently shared content (webpage/video/presentation) immediately
Preconditions: Host is actively sharing content; attendee joins after share started.
Steps:
1) Host starts sharing
2) Attendee joins
3) Observe
Expected Result: Attendee sees the shared content upon join; no blank state; consistent with other viewers.

Scenario / Title: Private chat between two users works during a stream meeting
Preconditions: Meeting is live; private chat feature enabled; two users are present.
Steps:
1) User A opens private chat with User B
2) Send message
3) User B replies
Expected Result: Messages are delivered only to the intended recipient; correct author/time; no leakage to others.

Scenario / Title: Private chat is not visible to host/others unless they are in the chat
Preconditions: User A and User B have private messages; Host is present.
Steps:
1) Host checks chat views
2) Verify private messages are not accessible
Expected Result: Host/others cannot view private messages between A and B; access is properly restricted.

Scenario / Title: Host can run a test stream from the platform dashboard
Preconditions: Host has access to dashboard; meeting exists and is within allowed test window.
Steps:
1) Go to dashboard
2) Click Test stream
3) Verify preview/stream status
Expected Result: Test stream starts successfully; host can verify audio/video/content; test does not publish to attendees unless intended.

Scenario / Title: Attendees cannot access dashboard test stream
Preconditions: Attendee account without host privileges.
Steps: 1) Attempt to access dashboard test stream URL/entry point
Expected Result: Access denied or feature hidden; attendee cannot start/see host-only test tools.

Scenario / Title: Recording is available on demand in the platform for the stream meeting
Preconditions: Recording feature is enabled for the meeting; meeting has been live for some time.
Steps:
1) Start recording (if manual) or confirm auto recording
2) End/stop recording
3) Navigate to recordings area
Expected Result: Recording appears in platform with correct metadata; playback works; download/view options follow permissions.

Scenario / Title: Recording is available from the lobby (as specified) after processing
Preconditions: A recording exists and is processed; lobby shows recordings for this meeting.
Steps:
1) Go to lobby
2) Open meeting recordings
3) Play recording
Expected Result: Recording is visible in lobby; playback works; attendee permissions are enforced.

Scenario / Title: Recording access respects permissions (unauthorized user cannot view)
Preconditions: Recording exists; user is not eligible for the event or lacks access.
Steps: 1) Attempt to open recording from lobby/platform
Expected Result: Access is denied; no content leakage; clear messaging.

Scenario / Title: Attendance is tracked for users who join the stream meeting
Preconditions: Attendance tracking is enabled; at least 3 users join.
Steps:
1) Host starts meeting
2) Users join
3) End meeting
4) View attendance report
Expected Result: Report lists users who joined; join events are captured correctly.

Scenario / Title: Attendance report does not include dwell time (only presence/attendance)
Preconditions: Meeting has join/leave events; attendance report available.
Steps:
1) User joins then leaves and re-joins
2) View attendance report fields
Expected Result: Report does not show dwell-time metrics; fields align with “no dwell time” requirement.

Scenario / Title: Short network interruption during live stream: attendee can recover playback without duplicating attendance
Preconditions: Live stream is running; attendee is watching.
Steps:
1) Disconnect network for ~20s
2) Reconnect
3) Observe playback and roster/attendance
Expected Result: Playback recovers (auto or via clear CTA); no duplicate participant entries; attendance remains correct.

Scenario / Title: Unauthenticated/unauthorized user cannot join the stream meeting
Preconditions: User not logged in or not part of the event; meeting has a join entry point.
Steps:
1) Attempt to access join URL
2) Attempt to enter the meeting
Expected Result: User is redirected to login or shown access denied; cannot view stream content.
